seo.title: Costa Rica Summer Program | Pacific Discovery
seo.description: Costa Rica in 4 weeks: an organic farm stay, rainforest hikes, surf lessons in Uvita, a Golfo Dulce kayak expedition, wildlife rescue volunteering and Pacuare rafting. Ages 17–22.

hero.headline: A summer of hiking, paddling and wildlife care in Costa Rica

itinerary.heading: Week by week
itinerary.note: This is a guide to what you can expect to do on program. The order in which activities occur might vary. Itineraries are subject to change.

weeks.title: Organic farm & Los Campesinos
weeks.location: San José → Villa Nueva Naranjo → Naranjito, Costa Rica
weeks.body:
You’ll meet your Program Instructors in San José, then we transfer to a working organic farm in Villa Nueva Naranjo for glamping and orientation. A spice tour introduces local spices, flowers and medicinal plants, and we spend a day in Manuel Antonio National Park.

Next we hike 8 km from Brisas del Nara to Los Campesinos Ecolodge, finishing with a trapiche tour and a welcome barbecue. Horseback riding, the Los Campesinos trails and a soccer game follow, then a volunteer project in the community.
weeks.imageAlt: Student carrying a basket of fruit on a forest path

weeks.title: Ranchos Tinamú & surf in Uvita
weeks.location: Naranjito → San Isidro de Dota → Uvita, Costa Rica
weeks.body:
We hike 16 km from Los Campesinos to Ranchos Tinamú in San Isidro de Dota. Here we spend a day tree planting, take a waterfall hike and head out on a night tour.

Then it’s down to the coast and Cabinas El Tecal in Uvita for surf lessons. Between sessions we hike the Cola de Ballena, visit Nauyaca waterfall and explore Dominical, before transferring to Golfito for an afternoon of kayak expedition practice.
weeks.imageAlt: Surfer carrying a board through the whitewater

weeks.title: Golfo Dulce kayaking & wildlife rescue
weeks.location: Golfito → Golfo Dulce → Alajuela, Costa Rica
weeks.body:
Our kayak expedition covers 15 km on the Golfo Dulce to Dolphin Quest Camp, then 10 km with a snorkel stop. Back in Golfito we kayak and snorkel some more and explore the town.

After a final paddle we transfer to Guácima near Alajuela for an introduction to the animal rescue center. We spend the rest of the week volunteering here, helping with daily care, food preparation and enrichment for animals like sloths and howler monkeys.
weeks.imageAlt: Young sloths wrapped in a towel in a blue tub

weeks.title: Yoga retreat, Pacuare River & farewell
weeks.location: Alajuela → Sarapiquí → Pacuare → San José, Costa Rica
weeks.body:
We transfer to Epic Adventure Lodge in Sarapiquí for our yoga retreat, followed by a free day.

Then we head to the Pacuare River and raft in to Pacuare River Eco Lodge. From the lodge we hike to an Indigenous village and hold our program wrap, before rafting out and returning to San José, where students depart from Juan Santamaría International Airport.

day.heading: What a typical day looks like

notes.title: Free time
notes.body: Each week there is some designated free time to catch up on email and laundry, rest and explore with others in the group.

notes.title: Phones & wifi
notes.body: We encourage flight mode so you stay present. Wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns.

notes.title: Fitness needed
notes.body: High activity level, but no experience is required. Anyone with average fitness and enthusiasm for the outdoors will be fine. Expect hikes of 8 km and 16 km, a multi-day kayak expedition, rafting, surfing and some physical work on conservation projects, like cleaning animal enclosures and planting trees.

items.title: Sustainability on working farms
items.body: A spice tour on a working organic farm, a volunteer project in the Naranjito community and tree planting at Ranchos Tinamú.

items.title: Wildlife rescue and rehabilitation
items.body: Days at an animal rescue center helping with daily care, food preparation and enrichment for rescued animals.

items.title: Optional college credit
items.body: Earn college credit through the University of Montana. 529 education funds can be used to pay for your credits and your Pacific Discovery program tuition.

faq.heading: Questions we get about this program

items.q: How fit do I need to be?
items.a: This is a high activity program, but no experience is required. Anyone with average fitness and enthusiasm for the outdoors will be fine. Expect hikes of 8 km and 16 km, kayaking, rafting and surfing, plus some physical work on conservation projects. There is downtime scheduled between the expeditions.

items.q: Do I need to know how to surf, kayak or raft?
items.a: No. You’ll have surf lessons in Uvita, an afternoon of practice in Golfito before the kayak expedition, and the Pacuare rafting needs no previous experience.
Mostly ecolodges, lodges and cabins, plus glamping on an organic farm, Dolphin Quest Camp during the kayak expedition and nights at the wildlife rescue center.

items.q: What will I do at the wildlife rescue center?
items.a: You’ll help with daily care, food preparation and enrichment activities for animals like sloths and howler monkeys, and physical work like cleaning out enclosures.

Tuition covers all in-country transport, accommodation, meals, and the activities and entry fees in the itinerary. It doesn't cover international flights, visas, travel insurance, spending money, optional college credit or optional activities.

items.q: How much spending money should I bring?
items.a: About $100 a week for snacks, laundry, personal shopping and optional activities. It varies from student to student.

items.q: Can I stay in touch with home?
items.a: Yes. We encourage keeping phones on flight mode so you stay present, and wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns. There will also be a photo album that students and instructors can upload photos and video to, so parents and caregivers can stay up to date.

items.q: Do I need a passport or visa?
items.a: Your passport must be valid for more than 6 months after the program ends. All the information you need in regard to visas will be available in your student portal.

safety.heading: For parents: how we keep students safe

items.title: 24/7 Emergency Line
items.body: Parents, students and instructors can reach a real person at any hour. Every call is logged and passed to our on-call staff member by phone.

items.title: Wilderness First Aid & Live Risk Assessment
items.body: All our instructors hold Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certification and have extensive training in group leadership and risk management.

items.title: Accredited Safety Systems
items.body: Our safety systems are assessed and accredited by the Gap Year Association (USA), Year Out Group (UK) and OutdoorsMark (NZ). Students on Go Overseas voted us one of the top gap year providers for safety.

items.title: Insurance & Health
items.body: Comprehensive travel insurance is required, covering medical costs and emergency evacuation. Check vaccinations with your doctor, and pack a first-aid kit and any personal medication. Our instructors can't legally give students any medication.
